epics.title: Dragoman — standalone harness project
epics.description:
A fork of Nous Research's hermes-agent, run as its own project on its own service, not as a mind nested inside hive-edge-minds. The hive is a source of parts, not a container: where hive_mind has infrastructure Hermes lacks, we bolt that piece on; where Hermes already has it, we use Hermes'. Working checkouts read 2026-09-02: ~/Storage/Dev/hermes-agent, ~/Storage/Dev/deepseek-harness, ~/Storage/Dev/openclaw. Not to be confused with the Hermes-agent backlog epic, which is about cribbing Hermes' ideas into Skippy's Claude harness — different project, no shared work.

Why a fork rather than a build: tools are not the provider's. Every serious harness defines its own tool set once, in its own vocabulary, and translates on the way out; what differs per provider is the envelope (Anthropic Messages, OpenAI chat completions, OpenAI Responses) and the JSON Schema dialect the vendor's validator accepts. Hermes keeps an internal OpenAI-style canonical format (run_agent.py AIAgent), its own tool list (toolsets.py), and four transports under agent/transports/ — anthropic.py, chat_completions.py, codex.py for Responses, bedrock.py — each with a convert_tools(); providers are declarative plugins (providers/base.py ProviderProfile). DeepSeek dsh has a cleaner plugin architecture but only a DeepSeek adapter in tree: more design, less coverage. OpenClaw has the widest provider matrix, 93 files in packages/ai/src/providers, and is the reference for which quirks are real.

The trained 'agent interpreter' idea is answered and dropped. OpenClaw's packages/tool-call-repair handles exactly the case it was proposed for — a weak model emitting a tool call as plain text, Harmony channel markers, or XML-ish tags — with a deterministic grammar plus a name resolver onto the allowed tool names, running only when the normal parse yields nothing. That is also the answer to the latency worry. Collected tool-call data belongs in fine-tuning a model to emit correctly, not in an inference-time interpreter.
epics.requirements:
The gap analysis, verified by reading both trees, is the bolt-on list and nothing else is. Memory: Hermes has a pluggable provider architecture (agent/memory_provider.py, agent/memory_manager.py) whose built-in provider is two capped markdown files, plus FTS5 session search and load-time injection scanning — merge, not replace; lucent plugs in as a provider and Hermes' search, prefetch, injection scanning and lifecycle hooks are kept. Identity: Hermes has a load_soul_identity flag and file-based identity — medium gap, no soul in a graph, no self-reflect, no proposal review. Provider routing: Hermes goes direct to vendor or OpenRouter — medium gap, our inference proxy owns the provider and model tables and Hermes must route through it. Multi-mind: delegate_tool.py spawns subagents — medium gap, no broker, no peer minds, no inter-mind messaging. Browser terminal: Hermes has a TUI and a web dashboard using xterm for output but no pty websocket route — bolt ours on. Console management: Hermes has its own React dashboard — bolt ours on, the hive console is the management surface, do not build a second one. HITL gating: none found — small-to-medium, hive-tools' approval surface. Surfaces, skills, cron, sandboxed execution and training capture: Hermes wins outright, leave them alone. Voice: none known, compare against our TTS pipeline before assuming. Context compaction: Hermes has a pluggable context engine whose compaction splits the session and rotates the session id — structurally the same move as our rotation, so our carry-forward composition becomes a context-engine plugin.

The honest read: Hermes is more full-featured than our harness in every dimension except memory, identity and multi-mind. Those three are the project. Everything else we leave alone. Deliberately not in scope: replacing Hermes' surfaces, skills, cron, sandboxes or trajectory capture with ours. If ours is better at one of those, that is a separate finding and a separate document.
epics.acceptance_criteria: Story order: 01 fork, pin and stand it up, blocking on nothing; 02 route every provider through the inference proxy, blocking on 01; 03 memory and context merge, blocking on 01; 04 identity, blocking on 03; 05 hive console, web terminal and interop, blocking on 01; 06 provider-quirk hardening, blocking on 02. 01 and 02 give a running agent on our own inference. 03 and 04 make it one of ours rather than a stranger with our API keys. 05 puts him in the hive console and the browser terminal and lets him talk to the other minds. 06 makes the portability claim true for the models that misbehave. Skippy inherits the four rotation improvements afterwards, tracked as its own epic.
epics.qa_tests: Each story carries its own acceptance checklist; those are the tests. The through-line: a turn runs on our own inference with no vendor key in Dragoman's environment, memory lands in lucent under Dragoman's own mind_id, he answers as himself on a cold session, he appears in the hive console, and a named open-weight model that could not call a tool can.

features.title: Dragoman 01 — fork, pin, and stand it up
features.description:
Blocks on nothing. Blocks everything. A fork under Daniel's GitHub, running on this workstation as its own service, answering on one surface, with nothing bolted on yet — the walking skeleton.

Done 2026-09-04. Repo danielstewart77/dragoman, private, not a GitHub fork: upstream is MIT and a GitHub fork of a public repo is public, while the hive integration work is not. The upstream remote points at Nous, so rebasing is unchanged. Pin 63279301bcbdc185c1b07b98a9312eb0c862f26d, 2026-09-03, recorded in the README header; main sits on the pin and hive carries the work. Checkout ~/Storage/Dev/dragoman, installed with ./setup-hermes.sh (uv, Python 3.11, its own venv). HERMES_HOME is ~/Storage/Dev/dragoman/hermes_home, gitignored along with .proxy-key; nothing was written to ~/.hermes. Identity in hermes_home/.env: MIND_NAME=dragoman, MIND_ID=39369381-0700-4203-b742-f6c9555adcc7, no soul. Proxy client Dragoman (id 10, kind mind, unprivileged) with its own key, configured as provider custom against http://127.0.0.1:8899/v1. terminal.cwd is the project directory — without it the agent operated from /home/daniel and read the home CLAUDE.md. Service hermes-gateway.service as a systemd user unit, generated by hermes gateway install, enabled, linger on, with local settings in the drop-in dragoman.conf so a --force reinstall does not eat them. Verified: a tool-calling turn against qwen35-131k through the proxy ran pwd and read README.md correctly. Telegram token and allowed users in the repo .env, gitignored; the gateway connects and polls as @hivemind_dragoman_bot.
features.requirements: Fork NousResearch/hermes-agent, keeping upstream as a second remote so a rebase stays legible. Branch hive off the pinned upstream commit; master tracks upstream; the pinned SHA and date go in the README header. The checkout is a fresh clone at ~/Storage/Dev/dragoman, not the read-only ~/Storage/Dev/hermes-agent reference. Install per Hermes' own instructions (setup-hermes.sh, uv.lock) — do not invent a build, it has one. HERMES_HOME set explicitly to a path inside the project, never the default ~/.hermes. The name is dragoman; mint its UUID once and put it in configuration; it is not Skippy and must not answer as him; it starts with no soul and Daniel writes one before first real use. Deploy as a user systemd unit matching the inference proxy's pattern on this host — not docker for the first install, not root. One surface for this story: Telegram, on its own bot token, because a second process on Skippy's token fights him for updates.
features.acceptance_criteria: The fork exists, is pinned, and the pin is recorded in its README — done. ~/Storage/Dev/dragoman runs from a clean checkout with no manual patching outside the repo — done. Nothing is written to ~/.hermes — done. A tool call executes, file read and a shell command at minimum — done. Still open: the service starts under systemd as daniel, survives a reboot and logs to journald; a message on its own Telegram bot gets an answer with Skippy's Telegram conversation unaffected; and it answers with its own name rather than Skippy's.
features.qa_tests: The tool-calling turn against qwen35-131k through the proxy running pwd and reading README.md is the verification that landed. What remains is a reboot test, a real Telegram exchange, and a cold-session identity check. Three known gaps are recorded rather than guessed at: the unit is enabled with linger but not reboot-tested; gpt-5.6 does not work through this proxy path because the proxy sent it to the Codex Responses endpoint and upstream refused — that model is not available on a ChatGPT account, so the default is qwen35-131k until story 02 settles model routing; and project-context discovery is skipped with a warning on every start, because Dragoman's own checkout is a Hermes install tree which the prompt builder deliberately refuses to treat as project context — harmless until he is given a workspace directory of his own.

features.title: Dragoman 02 — route every provider through the inference proxy
features.description:
Blocks on 01. The fork gets its models from our inference proxy, not from vendor SDKs holding vendor keys and not from OpenRouter. One credential, one place that knows which models exist, one request log.

Current state on our side: the proxy owns providers and models (~/Storage/Dev/inference-proxy, app/deployments.py, the providers and models tables). A provider row carries a host, a credential, and one path per wire shape; the path is chosen by the endpoint a request arrives on. Two listings exist today and each is a harness view — /v1/anthropic/models for Claude-shaped clients, /v1/models for OpenAI-shaped ones — and per-model harnesses visibility withholds what is named.

The problem: Hermes speaks all three wires, with an adapter per wire, so neither existing listing is right for it. Asking for the Anthropic view hides every OpenAI-shaped model and vice versa.
features.requirements: Add a third wire label, hermes, and a listing endpoint /v1/hermes/models returning the union of models the calling credential may address across every enabled provider. Each row names its provider and its wire — anthropic, openai_chat, openai_responses. In the fork, add a ProviderProfile for the proxy — one profile, not one per vendor — which reads the wire off the model's row and sets api_mode accordingly, the field Hermes' own transports already dispatch on; this is the whole point of forking Hermes rather than writing a harness, in that the mechanism exists and we are supplying a profile. Model selection stays Hermes' own (hermes model), listing what the proxy offers rather than a hardcoded catalog, via ProviderProfile.fetch_models(). The harnesses visibility field gains hermes as an addressable value so a model can be withheld from Dragoman specifically. Strip the upstream provider profiles we will not use, so a misconfiguration cannot silently fall back to OpenRouter with an ambient key.
features.acceptance_criteria: /v1/hermes/models lists Anthropic-hosted, OpenAI-hosted and Ollama-hosted models in one response, each naming its provider and wire. hermes model inside the fork lists exactly that set. Selecting an Anthropic-hosted model and running a turn with tools reaches the Anthropic Messages endpoint, confirmed in the proxy's request log rather than ours. Selecting an OpenAI-hosted model reaches the Responses endpoint, same confirmation. Selecting an Ollama-hosted open-weight model answers and calls a tool. Switching provider mid-project is a model selection and nothing else — no code change, no restart, no config edit. No request leaves this host to any endpoint other than the proxy, verified by revoking every direct vendor key from Dragoman's environment and confirming it still works. A model marked withheld from hermes, or whose provider is disabled, does not appear.
features.qa_tests: The strongest test is the key revocation: strip every direct vendor key from Dragoman's environment and confirm he still answers — anything that still works is going through the proxy. The per-wire confirmations are read from the proxy's own request log, not from Dragoman's side, because Dragoman reporting which endpoint it believes it reached proves nothing.

features.title: Dragoman 03 — memory and context
features.description:
Blocks on 01, blocks 04. Nothing Hermes does is dropped. Nothing the hive does is dropped. Where the two overlap, merge and keep the stronger behaviour.

Both extension points already exist — use them, do not fork around them. Memory: agent/memory_provider.py is an abstract pluggable provider; agent/memory_manager.py orchestrates it and permits one external provider at a time; plugins live in plugins/memory/<name>/, activated by the memory.provider config key. Its lifecycle is initialize, system_prompt_block, prefetch(query), sync_turn(user, assistant), get_tool_schemas, handle_tool_call, shutdown, with optional hooks on_turn_start, on_session_end, on_session_switch, on_pre_compress, on_memory_write, on_delegation and backup_paths. Context: agent/context_engine.py is an abstract pluggable engine selected by context.engine in config, one active, owning when compaction fires and what compaction is, with lifecycle on_session_start, update_from_response(usage), should_compress(), compact, and it may expose its own tools. Build two plugins — plugins/memory/lucent/ and plugins/context_engine/rotation/ — with no fork surgery in either case.

Correction to a prior assumption: Hermes' compaction is not summarise-in-place. compress_context in agent/conversation_compression.py runs the compressor, splits the SQLite session, rotates the session id, and notifies context engines and memory providers. That is structurally the same move as our rotation. Treat the two as one mechanism with two implementations, not as two different ideas.
features.requirements:
The merge matrix, with disposition keep-Hermes, keep-ours, merge or audit. Memory store: merge — lucent is the store of record via the provider plugin, keeping the built-in markdown files as a small local working set only if an audit shows they earn it, otherwise retiring them. Recall injection: merge — a session-start frozen block from a decay-weighted lucent recall plus per-turn contextual injection for what the turn is actually about, measuring and recording the prefix-cache cost of the per-turn part. Pre-turn recall: keep Hermes, because background prefetch is strictly better than our synchronous per-turn hook. Post-turn capture: merge — sync_turn as the entry point with our classification pipeline and data-class routing behind it. Classification and tiers: keep ours, Hermes has no equivalent. Conversation search: keep Hermes — FTS5 over every past session with anchored scroll windows and bookends at zero LLM cost is a different capability from vector search and they complement. Injection defence on recall: keep Hermes — _sanitize_entries_for_snapshot scans every entry against tools/threat_patterns.py at load time and substitutes a [BLOCKED] placeholder, and it gets applied to lucent recall too. Compaction trigger: keep Hermes' — should_compress() on real token usage from update_from_response beats our transcript-bytes-over-a-constant heuristic. Compaction action: merge — our carry-forward composition inside their engine, fired by their trigger. Pre-switch extraction: merge and rename — we rotate rather than compress, so on_pre_compress becomes on_pre_switch and lucent extraction runs there. Session switch: merge — their single hook, our staged discipline where a surface needs it. Session end: merge. Subagent observation, memory write mirroring and backup: keep Hermes, we have none of the three. Identity: keep ours, see story 04. Turn prologue: keep Hermes — agent/turn_context.py is one place that builds every per-turn value, and it is where our injections attach.

The carry-forward audit is resolved. Already ours and kept unchanged: structured project extraction with goal, success criteria, phases and status; in-flight work and next step; state extraction carrying files edited, recent edits, decisions made and open questions; data-class tagging on every extracted project; projects written to the knowledge graph as memories rather than only into the prompt; late-turn folding so turns typed during the rotation window reach the successor; model-aware thresholds; and waiting for transcript quiescence before reading. Hermes' resolved-and-pending question tracking is already covered by decisions_made and open_questions in STATE_SCHEMA, so no work. Four things Hermes has that we do not, all four to be added: iterative summary, filter-safe preamble and historical headings, token-budget tail protection, and a tool-output pruning pre-pass.

Extraction model: run the structured extraction calls against Ollama through the inference proxy, never against a bare Ollama daemon — the proxy is the only door. Do not port _audit_claude_md from Skippy's rotation_check.py; that is a Skippy habit and Dragoman does not get it.
features.acceptance_criteria: The memory tool schema the model sees is unchanged, and an entry the model saves lands in lucent. Every provider lifecycle hook is implemented and each one is exercised by a test. A write carries Dragoman's own mind_id from configuration. A standing-tier write without source=always-remember is refused and the refusal surfaces. An ephemeral-classified chunk is discarded and never written. A recalled chunk containing instruction-shaped text is blocked before it enters the prompt. Session start injects a decay-weighted lucent block that does not change mid-session. Recall runs as background prefetch and does not add latency to the turn. Rotation fires on real token counts reported by the provider, not on file size. A rotation extracts to lucent through on_pre_switch before context is discarded, and the extraction is present in the graph afterwards. The carry-forward carries all four added capabilities, each with a test. A subagent's work is observed by the parent through on_delegation and reaches memory. session_search finds a message from a session that rotated away. A lucent outage degrades to answering without memory, never to a failed turn. Every extraction call reaches Ollama through the proxy, confirmed in the proxy's request log.
features.qa_tests: The four carry-forward capabilities each get their own test: a fact established before the previous rotation survives this one; the summary's headings do not read as instructions; a tail of oversized turns does not crowd out the summary; and tool output is pruned before the summariser sees it. The degradation test matters as much as the happy path — a lucent outage must answer without memory rather than fail the turn. Confirm extraction routing from the proxy's request log, not from Dragoman's side.

stories.title: Write plugins/memory/lucent with the full provider lifecycle
stories.description: Not the minimum: prefetch, sync_turn, on_session_end, on_session_switch, on_pre_switch, on_memory_write, on_delegation and backup_paths.
stories.requirements: Every hook implemented, each exercised by a test.
stories.acceptance_criteria: No hook is a stub.
stories.qa_tests: Each lifecycle hook has a test that fails if the hook is removed. A hook that is implemented but never called by Hermes is a finding, not a pass.

stories.acceptance_criteria: An ephemeral chunk is never written anywhere.
stories.qa_tests: An ephemeral-classified chunk produces no row in lucent. A standing-tier write without source=always-remember is refused by the server and the refusal surfaces to the caller rather than being swallowed.

stories.description: _sanitize_entries_for_snapshot already does this for Hermes' own entries, substituting a [BLOCKED] placeholder. Apply it to lucent recall too.
stories.requirements: Every chunk recalled from lucent is scanned before it enters the prompt.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Instruction-shaped recalled text is blocked, not injected.
stories.qa_tests: A chunk seeded into lucent containing instruction-shaped text comes back as [BLOCKED] rather than reaching the prompt. A benign chunk is unaffected.

stories.title: Rename on_pre_compress to on_pre_switch in the fork
stories.description: We rotate rather than compress. Update the provider ABC and its call sites.
stories.requirements: The ABC and every call site renamed.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The hook's name matches what it does.
stories.qa_tests: A provider implementing on_pre_switch is called at rotation. No call site still names on_pre_compress.

stories.title: Write plugins/context_engine/rotation
stories.description: Fire on Hermes' real-token trigger. Compose the carry-forward from the union the memory plugin produces.
stories.requirements: Rotation fires on real token counts from update_from_response, not on transcript bytes over a chars-per-token constant.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The trigger is the provider's own reported usage.
stories.qa_tests: A session whose reported usage crosses the threshold rotates; one whose transcript is large but whose reported usage is small does not. That second case is what distinguishes the real trigger from our old heuristic.

stories.title: Add the four carry-forward improvements to the composition
stories.description: Iterative summary input, filter-safe preamble and historical headings, token-budget tail, and tool-output pruning pre-pass. These are the same four Skippy later inherits.
stories.requirements: All four, each with a test.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Each of the four has an observable effect.
stories.qa_tests: A fact from before the previous rotation survives. No heading reads as an instruction. Six oversized turns leave the summary intact. Tool output is absent from the summariser's input.

stories.title: Keep session_search_tool.py and its FTS5 index exactly as it is
stories.description: Keep Hermes. FTS5 over every past session with anchored scroll windows and bookends at zero LLM cost is a different capability from vector search; they complement.
stories.requirements: Unchanged.
stories.acceptance_criteria: It keeps working across rotations.
stories.qa_tests: session_search finds a message from a session that rotated away. That is the case vector recall cannot cover.

stories.title: Expose the memory tool schema unchanged to the model
stories.description: So Hermes' own guidance text, tests and skills keep working while the bytes land in lucent.
stories.requirements: Schema unchanged; destination changed.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The model sees the same tool and the data goes somewhere else.
stories.qa_tests: The schema the model receives is byte-identical to upstream's. An entry the model saves through it lands in lucent.

stories.title: Degrade on a lucent outage rather than failing the turn
stories.description: A lucent outage answers without memory.
stories.requirements: Never a failed turn.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The turn completes.
stories.qa_tests: With lucent stopped, a turn completes and the reply says nothing about an error. With lucent back, memory returns. A turn that fails is the defect.

stories.title: Route extraction calls through the inference proxy
stories.description: Against Ollama through the proxy, never a bare daemon. The proxy is the only door.
stories.requirements: Every extraction call goes through the proxy.
stories.acceptance_criteria: No direct daemon call.
stories.qa_tests: Confirmed in the proxy's request log, not from Dragoman's side. Ollama binds loopback with the Host check on, so a bare-daemon call would fail anyway — but the log is what proves the routing.

stories.title: Audit whether the built-in markdown memory files earn their keep
stories.description: An audit row is a task, not a question for Daniel. Keep them as a small local working set only if the audit shows they earn it; otherwise retire them.
stories.requirements: A decision with evidence.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Kept with a reason or retired.
stories.qa_tests: Not code. The artifact is the audit's finding.

stories.title: Measure the prefix-cache cost of per-turn injection
stories.description: Hermes freezes its recall snapshot at session start deliberately, to preserve the prefix cache. Our per-turn contextual injection breaks that. The merge keeps both, so the cost has to be known rather than assumed acceptable.
stories.requirements: Measure it and record the figure.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The cost is a number, not an impression.
stories.qa_tests: A measured comparison of turns with and without per-turn injection, reading the provider's own cache-hit reporting.

features.title: Dragoman 04 — identity
features.description:
Blocks on 03. The gap: Hermes has a load_soul_identity flag and file-based identity. The hive keeps a mind's canonical soul in the lucent graph, seeds it into the system prompt, and lets the mind revise its own soul through a review flow — a sub-mind flags something identity-shaping and the mind itself decides whether it goes in.

Mind identity is configuration, not a constant. Hermes has no concept of a mind_id and does not need one, since nothing upstream is multi-mind. The value is ours and it enters through the lucent client built in story 03, so adapting Hermes costs nothing: no fork surgery, no upstream concept to fight. Make it a configuration value read at startup, never a constant in the code. Name and UUID come from configuration. The name is dragoman. The project must be able to host a second mind later without a rewrite.
features.requirements: A Mind node in the graph keyed to Dragoman's UUID, exactly as every hive mind has — without it, recall answers as whoever the graph thinks owns the memories, a failure we have already had once and diagnosed. Start with no soul: Dragoman runs plain through testing, Daniel writes the soul seed before first real use, and until then the seed file is absent and the graph holds no soul_values for this mind; an empty soul is a valid state and must not raise. Session-start prompt composition reads the soul from the graph when one exists and composes without it when none does, injecting it alongside the memory block from story 03 — one composition step, two sources. self-reflect and identity-proposal review as skills, written for Hermes' own skill format, since it has tools/skills_sync.py and skill_manager_tool.py and honours the agentskills.io layout, so this is authoring content rather than building machinery. Soul writes stay guarded the same way they are for hive minds: this agent decides its own soul and nothing else writes it.
features.acceptance_criteria: A Mind node exists for Dragoman, keyed to its UUID, and recall returns its memories rather than another mind's. The soul reaches the system prompt from the graph, and editing the graph changes the next session's answers with no code change. Dragoman can run self-reflect and a proposal review end to end. A soul write from anything other than Dragoman's own review flow is refused. Dragoman answers as itself, with its own name, on a cold session with no conversation history. A mind with no soul values starts, answers, and rotates without error.
features.qa_tests: The empty-soul case is as important as the populated one: a mind with no soul_values must start, answer and rotate without error, because that is the state Dragoman lives in through testing. The identity test is read, not asserted — a cold session with no history answering as Dragoman rather than as Skippy.

stories.title: Create a Mind node in the graph keyed to Dragoman's UUID
stories.description: Exactly as every hive mind has. Without it, recall answers as whoever the graph thinks owns the memories — a failure we have already had once and diagnosed, when Hex answered as Ada.
stories.requirements: A Mind node keyed to the UUID.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Recall returns Dragoman's memories, not another mind's.
stories.qa_tests: A memory written by Dragoman is recalled by Dragoman and is absent from another mind's recall. The Hex failure is the exact shape to test against.

stories.title: Make an empty soul a valid state
stories.description: Dragoman starts with no soul and runs plain through testing. The seed file is absent and the graph holds no soul_values for him.
stories.requirements: An empty soul must not raise.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A mind with no soul values starts, answers and rotates without error.
stories.qa_tests: With no soul file and no soul_values in the graph: start, take a turn, and rotate. All three complete. This is the normal state for weeks, so it cannot be the untested path.

stories.title: Compose the system prompt from the graph's soul plus the memory block
stories.description: One composition step, two sources. Reads the soul when one exists and composes without it when none does.
stories.requirements: Soul from the graph, memory from story 03, in one step.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Editing the graph changes the next session's answers with no code change.
stories.qa_tests: Change a soul value in the graph and read the next cold session's answer. A soul-less run composes the memory block alone.

stories.title: Author self-reflect and proposal review as Hermes-format skills
stories.description: Hermes has tools/skills_sync.py and skill_manager_tool.py and honours the agentskills.io layout, so this is authoring content, not building machinery.
stories.requirements: Both skills in Hermes' own format, runnable end to end.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Dragoman can run self-reflect and a proposal review end to end.
stories.qa_tests: A self-reflect run produces a proposal; a review decides it. Judged by reading the result, since the output is a model's judgement about identity.

stories.title: Guard soul writes to Dragoman's own review flow
stories.description: This agent decides its own soul; nothing else writes it. Same guard hive minds have.
stories.requirements: A write from anything other than the review flow is refused.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The refusal is real, not advisory.
stories.qa_tests: A soul write attempted outside the review flow is refused. One through the flow succeeds. The refusal surfaces rather than being swallowed.

features.title: Dragoman 05 — hive console, web terminal, and interop
features.description:
Blocks on 01, independent of 03 and 04, can run in parallel. Dragoman is managed from the hive console and reachable through the hive's browser terminal, the same as every other mind. Hermes' own React dashboard at web/ is not the management surface — do not build a second one.

What Hermes already has: an aiohttp API server (gateway/platforms/api_server.py) exposing health, models, skills, toolsets, a full session API (list, create, get, patch, delete, messages, fork, chat, streaming chat) and jobs. Its web/ dashboard uses xterm for terminal-styled output, but there is no pty websocket route and no tmux-backed terminal; its interactive terminal is the local TUI (ui-tui), not a browser one. Our web terminal is the better surface and there is nothing upstream to merge with it.
features.requirements:
Routes Dragoman must expose, implemented on Hermes' existing API server rather than a second HTTP app, because the hive console speaks a fixed contract. GET /runtime for allowlisted configuration — name, mind id, harness, provider, default model. PATCH /runtime to set default_model and provider in one write, admin guarded, refusing with 503 when no admin token is configured. GET /models relaying the proxy's listing for Dragoman's own credential on the hermes endpoint from story 02, where an unreachable proxy yields an empty list and never an error. GET /skills, GET /skills/{name}/diff, POST /skills/{name}/install, POST /skills/{name}/write-back and DELETE /skills/{name} over $HERMES_HOME/skills, adapting the existing tools/skills_sync.py to report the same states the console renders: same, differs, not_installed, local_only, unreadable. GET /files/{tree}, GET /files/{tree}/content and PUT /files/{tree}/content where tree is skills or hooks and nothing else, judging containment on the resolved path rather than the spelling, with a save carrying a revision and a stale one refused with 409. WS /sessions/{id}/attach-pty as the browser terminal bridge. POST /broker/minds registration on every boot, read from Dragoman's own configuration file, so the file is authoritative and the broker row is a cache of it. Every route is admin guarded, reads included — a skills listing returns the full text of what Dragoman runs, on a port reachable across the LAN.

Browser terminal: follow the tmux-backed pattern already proven in hive-edge-mind-skippy/mind_templates/claude_cli.py spawn_pty. Start the Hermes TUI inside a tmux session on a dedicated socket, then attach a tmux attach-session -d client in a pty of the tile's geometry — the conversation lives in tmux and a tile is a client. setsid plus TIOCSCTTY so SIGWINCH reaches the app. Exact-match tmux targets, the = form, on every lookup. NUL heartbeat every 5 seconds. The process ends only on DELETE /sessions/{id}; a terminal is never collected for being unattached and a turn in flight survives a closed tab. Stamp HERMES_HOME and the provider environment into the pane and cache them on the handle. Determine, before writing the rotation half, whether the TUI can be launched against an existing session id — Hermes mints and persists its own session ids and hermes_state.py resolves resume ids, so this is expected to work; prove it, then wire the terminal to the same conversation the chat surface holds.

Rotation in the pane: the context engine from story 03 owns rotation. In a pane, swap with respawn-pane -k onto a fresh process carrying the seed, renaming and killing nothing, so the attached tmux client, the pty and the browser tile are never disturbed. The seed travels in a file the pane reads and deletes, capped at 120,000 bytes, never on the tmux command line. A seed that cannot be read starts the harness unseeded rather than on an empty prompt.

Interop: inbound, a route accepting an inter-mind message mapped onto a Hermes session, so Skippy or Ada can ask Dragoman something. Outbound, one Hermes tool for sending an inter-mind message. HITL, anything needing approval routes through hive-tools' existing surface — do not build a second approval path.
features.acceptance_criteria: Dragoman appears in the hive console's mind list after a boot, with his own mind id. The console's model picker offers Dragoman's models and saving writes both provider and model to his configuration file and then the broker row. The console's skills table shows correct states for Dragoman's skills, and installing a repo skill then re-listing reports same. The console's file editor opens and saves a file in both trees, and a stale revision is refused with 409. A path resolving outside both allowed roots is named in the response, not silently dropped, and cannot be opened. A browser tile attaches, the TUI paints, resize repaints, closing the tab does not end the conversation, and reattaching joins the same tmux session. A turn in flight survives a closed tab. Whether the terminal shares the chat surface's conversation is proven and stated, either way. A rotation in a pane keeps the tile, the session row and its label, and the user keeps typing in the same pane. Skippy can message Dragoman and get a reply; Dragoman can message Skippy unprompted. An action needing approval reaches Daniel through hive-tools. Every route refuses without an admin token, reads included. Nothing in the hive breaks when Dragoman's service is stopped.
features.qa_tests: Two acceptance items are unusual and deliberate. 'Whether the terminal shares the chat surface's conversation is proven and stated, either way' means the answer may be no — what is unacceptable is not knowing. And 'nothing in the hive breaks when Dragoman's service is stopped' is tested by stopping it and using the console, which is how a new mind's routes get folded into shapes that mean something else.

stories.title: Expose GET and PATCH /runtime on Hermes' API server
stories.description: Allowlisted configuration out; default_model and provider set in one write. Admin guarded, refusing with 503 when no admin token is configured rather than opening.
stories.requirements: Both routes, one write for both fields, 503 on no configured token.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The console's picker saves provider and model together.
stories.qa_tests: A PATCH naming both lands both in one write — a mind is never left holding a provider that does not host the model beside it. With no admin token configured, the route refuses with 503 rather than serving open.

stories.title: Relay the proxy's listing as GET /models
stories.description: For Dragoman's own credential, on the hermes endpoint from story 02.
stories.requirements: An unreachable proxy yields an empty list, never an error.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The console distinguishes 'nothing offered' from 'the mind is down'.
stories.qa_tests: With the proxy stopped, the route returns an empty list and a 200. With it running, the list matches /v1/hermes/models.

stories.title: Adapt tools/skills_sync.py to the console's five states
stories.description: same, differs, not_installed, local_only, unreadable — over $HERMES_HOME/skills. Plus diff, install, write-back and delete.
stories.requirements: The five states exactly, and all five routes.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Installing a repo skill then re-listing reports same.
stories.qa_tests: Each of the five states is reachable and reported correctly. unreadable is its own state rather than folding into absent, because the remedy for absence is to overwrite the directory and doing that to a merely-unreadable skill destroys it.

stories.title: Expose the two-tree file editor
stories.description: GET /files/{tree}, GET and PUT /files/{tree}/content. tree is skills or hooks and nothing else.
stories.requirements: Containment judged on the resolved path, not the spelling. A save carries a revision; a stale one is refused with 409.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A path resolving outside both allowed roots is named in the response, not silently dropped, and cannot be opened.
stories.qa_tests: A symlink aimed outside the allowed roots is named and refused. A save with a stale revision is refused with 409. A save with no revision is refused — one that is optional on the wire is not a check at all.

stories.title: Build the tmux-backed pty bridge
stories.description: WS /sessions/{id}/attach-pty, following the pattern proven in claude_cli.py spawn_pty. The TUI runs inside tmux on a dedicated socket; a tile is a client.
stories.requirements: setsid plus TIOCSCTTY so SIGWINCH reaches the app. Exact-match = tmux targets on every lookup. NUL heartbeat every 5 seconds. The process ends only on DELETE /sessions/{id}. HERMES_HOME and the provider environment stamped into the pane and cached on the handle.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A tile attaches, the TUI paints, resize repaints, closing the tab does not end the conversation, reattaching joins the same tmux session, and a turn in flight survives a closed tab.
stories.qa_tests: Resize the tile and the TUI repaints — without a controlling terminal, a resize sets winsize and signals nobody, which is what TIOCSCTTY fixes. Close the tab mid-turn and reattach: the turn completed. tmux targets are prefix-matched, so a lookup without the = form can answer for another session's pane.

stories.title: Prove whether the TUI can launch against an existing session id
stories.description: Hermes mints and persists its own session ids and hermes_state.py resolves resume ids, so this is expected to work. Prove it before writing the rotation half, then wire the terminal to the same conversation the chat surface holds.
stories.requirements: A proof either way, stated.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Whether the terminal shares the chat surface's conversation is proven and stated, either way.
stories.qa_tests: Launch the TUI against a session id the chat surface created and see whether it resumes that conversation. A negative answer, clearly stated, satisfies this — not knowing does not.

stories.title: Implement in-pane rotation with respawn-pane -k
stories.description: The context engine from story 03 owns rotation. In a pane, swap onto a fresh process carrying the seed, renaming and killing nothing, so the tmux client, the pty and the tile are never disturbed.
stories.requirements: The seed travels in a file the pane reads and deletes, capped at 120,000 bytes, never on the tmux command line. A seed that cannot be read starts the harness unseeded rather than on an empty prompt.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A rotation in a pane keeps the tile, the session row and its label, and the user keeps typing in the same pane.
stories.qa_tests: A rotation mid-conversation leaves the tile attached and the session id unchanged. A seed over the cap is trimmed to its tail in bytes, not characters — a carry-forward quoting a TUI transcript carries box-drawing and arrows, and a few per cent of those puts 120,000 characters over the kernel's 128 KiB argv limit. An unreadable seed opens unseeded rather than dead.

stories.title: Register on every boot via POST /broker/minds
stories.description: Read from Dragoman's own configuration file, so the file is authoritative and the broker row is a cache of it.
stories.requirements: Registration on every start. Failure logged, never fatal.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Dragoman appears in the console's mind list after a boot, with his own mind id.
stories.qa_tests: A boot produces the row. Editing the configuration file and restarting changes the row. A failed registration logs and the mind still runs.

stories.title: Wire inter-mind messaging both ways
stories.description: Inbound: a route accepting an inter-mind message, mapped onto a Hermes session. Outbound: one Hermes tool for sending one.
stories.requirements: Both directions.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Skippy can message Dragoman and get a reply; Dragoman can message Skippy unprompted.
stories.qa_tests: A message from Skippy reaches a Dragoman session and the reply comes back. An unprompted message from Dragoman reaches Skippy.

stories.title: Route HITL approvals through hive-tools
stories.description: Do not build a second approval path.
stories.requirements: Anything needing approval uses hive-tools' existing surface.
stories.acceptance_criteria: An action needing approval reaches Daniel through hive-tools.
stories.qa_tests: An approval-gated action produces a hive-tools approval request and blocks on it. No second approval surface exists.

stories.title: Admin-guard every route, reads included
stories.description: A skills listing returns the full text of what Dragoman runs, on a port reachable across the LAN.
stories.requirements: Every route, including reads.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Every route refuses without an admin token.
stories.qa_tests: Each route unauthenticated is refused. The skills listing in particular, since it returns source. A route added later that ships open is the failure mode, so the guard belongs in one place rather than per route.

stories.title: Confirm nothing in the hive breaks when Dragoman is stopped
stories.description: A new mind's routes must not be load-bearing for the rest of the hive.
stories.requirements: The console and the other minds work with Dragoman's service stopped.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Nothing breaks.
stories.qa_tests: Stop the service and use the console: the mind list renders, other minds answer, and Dragoman reads as down rather than as an error on an unrelated page. A 503 or a refusal from one mind must never be folded into a shape that means something else.

features.title: Dragoman 06 — provider-quirk hardening
features.description:
Blocks on 02. This is what makes 'any provider' true rather than aspirational.

The rule: every item lands driven by a real failure, with the failing model named in the commit. Nothing here is written speculatively.
features.requirements:
Tool schema scrubbing, referencing ~/Storage/Dev/openclaw/packages/ai/src/providers/: clean-for-gemini.ts for the JSON Schema keywords Google's Cloud Code Assist rejects (patternProperties, additionalProperties, $ref, $defs, minLength, pattern and more); openai-tool-schema-compat.ts for OpenAI strict-mode normalization; schema-keyword-strip.ts, the shared draft-07 through 2020-12 walker both build on; and clean-for-llamacpp-gbnf.ts for grammar-constrained local models. In the fork these belong on ProviderProfile — prepare_messages, and the transports' convert_tools — so a new provider declares its dialect rather than someone editing a transport.

Tool-call repair, referencing ~/Storage/Dev/openclaw/packages/tool-call-repair/: a weak open-weight model emits a tool call as plain assistant text, or wrapped in Harmony markers (<|channel|>, <|message|>, <|call|>), or in XML-ish function tags. OpenClaw parses these deterministically (grammar.ts, payload.ts) and promotes them to native tool-call blocks (promote.ts), resolving the emitted name onto the exact set of allowed tool names. Port as a Python module in the fork, invoked only when the transport's normal parse yields no tool call and the stop reason permits one. Never on the happy path — that is what keeps it free. This is the replacement for the trained-interpreter idea: if a model is bad enough that a grammar cannot recover it, the answer is a different model or a fine-tune that emits correctly, not an interpreter in the hot path.
features.acceptance_criteria: A named open-weight model that fails a tool call without repair succeeds with it, and the test names that model. Repair never fires on a turn whose tool call parsed normally — asserted, not assumed. An invented tool name matching no allowed tool is refused, not guessed. A provider that rejects a schema keyword is handled by a declaration on its profile, not a branch inside a transport. Every scrubber and repair rule names the model or provider that motivated it.
features.qa_tests: 'Repair never fires on the happy path' is asserted rather than assumed, because that assertion is what keeps repair free. 'An invented tool name matching no allowed tool is refused, not guessed' is the one that matters most — a name resolver that guesses turns a garbled call into a confident wrong action.

stories.title: Port the schema scrubbers onto ProviderProfile
stories.description: The four OpenClaw scrubbers — Gemini keyword rejection, OpenAI strict-mode normalization, the shared draft-07 through 2020-12 walker, and llamacpp GBNF — as declarations on the profile, reached through prepare_messages and the transports' convert_tools.
stories.requirements: A new provider declares its dialect rather than someone editing a transport.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A provider that rejects a schema keyword is handled by a declaration, not a branch inside a transport.
stories.qa_tests: A provider declaring a dialect has its schemas scrubbed accordingly, with no transport change. Every scrubber names the model or provider that motivated it — a scrubber with no named failure behind it is speculative and does not belong.

stories.title: Port tool-call repair as a Python module
stories.description: OpenClaw's deterministic grammar and payload parsing, promoting plain text, Harmony markers and XML-ish function tags to native tool-call blocks, with the emitted name resolved onto the exact set of allowed tool names.
stories.requirements: Invoked only when the transport's normal parse yields no tool call and the stop reason permits one. Never on the happy path.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A named open-weight model that fails a tool call without repair succeeds with it, and the test names that model. Repair never fires on a turn that parsed normally.
stories.qa_tests: The named model's failing turn succeeds with repair and the test names it. A normally-parsed turn does not invoke repair — asserted, not assumed, since that assertion is what keeps repair free. An invented tool name matching no allowed tool is refused rather than resolved to the nearest match.
